- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days) and model forecasts are high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative sharply (e.g., -1.00+ change) and model is still high, apply downward bias of 5–15% to reflect mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 10% above recent mean), reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is flat or mildly negative (0.00–0.33) and model is high, apply downward correction of 3–8% to align with mean reversion.  
- When news volume drops below 3.0, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts — treat as “low signal” zone, apply conservative adjustment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., >10% gap), assume sentiment overestimation — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment change is +0.67 or higher and model is low, consider upward bias of 5–10% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Always check if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average — if yes, apply downward correction unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
